senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; קוּן) [rhythmic song (v. P. Sm. 3603 s. v. קינא),] lamentation, dirge.
units: M. Kat. III, 9 ק׳ שאחת מדברת וכ׳ a lamentation is called ḳinah, when one speaks &c., v. עִינּוּי I.

<cite ref="Berakhot 7b:11">Ber. 7ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 3:1">Ps. III, 1</cite>) <he>מזמור … ק׳ וכ׳</he> ‘a song of David’? it ought to read, ‘a lamentation of David.’ <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2:8">Lam. R. to IV, 11</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 79:1">Ps. LXXIX, 1</cite>) <he>לא הוה קרא … בכי … נהי … ק׳ לאסף</he> the text ought to read, ‘a weeping of Asaf’, ‘an elegy of Asaf’, ‘a lamentation of Asaf’.

Ib. introd., end (ref. to Jer. IX, 9) על נאותיו … שנהפכו לק׳ over the beauties (pleasures) of Jacob which have been changed into mourning; a. fr.—[Gitt. 58ᵃ ועליהן קינה, v. קוּן.]—Pl. קִינוֹת, esp. ספר ק׳, מגילת ק׳, or ק׳ the Book of Lamentations.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 14b:8">B. Bath. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>סדרן … ק׳ וכ׳</he> the order of the books of Hagiographa is: Ruth … and Lamentations &c. Ib. 15ᵃ <he>ירמיה … וקנות</he> (corr. acc.) Jeremiah composed the book that bears his name, the Book of Kings, and Lamentations.
<cite ref="Chagigah 5b:3-16">Ḥag. 5ᵇ</cite> <he>רבי</he> … <he>ספר ק׳</he> Rabbi took up the Book of Lamentations and read &c.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 16:1:4">Y. Sabb. XVI, 15ᶜ</cite> top <he>היו … במגילת ק׳</he> were sitting and explaining the scroll of Lamentations; <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 4:25">Lam. R. to IV, 20</cite>; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 15:9">Lev. R. s. 15</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 8:8:6">Y. Pes. VIII, end, 36ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 1:5:4">Y. M. Kat. I, 80ᵈ</cite> top <he>קִינִים ונהי</he> lamentations and elegies.
